comments.author: @MartianMarvs
comments.text: I grew up surrounded by Pandan thicket in the Southern Philippines. As a child, me and my playmates would play with its branches and carved them into rubber band bullet toy guns. Every summer, my grandma and great grandma used their leaves and weaved them into colorful geometric designed mats after tedious work of boiling, drying, dyeing, shredding. We played in those trees and had fun memories in cushiony forest floor. The screw pine fruit scent filled the air and was so distinct and unforgettable. We never tried eating those fruits. Nobody told us it was edible. (Maybe because we had a lot of fruit trees nearby... or was it the scent? I wish I had a memory of its taste as a child)
